text:
tara: heads up — after updating redwoodctl on my MBP (macOS 13) we're seeing the login flow pop up a macOS Keychain prompt every ~30s while localserve is running. it blocks the process until someone clicks allow. reproducible for others?

evan: wow that's rough. did you upgrade from 0.9.x -> 0.10.x or clean install?

tara: upgraded from 0.9.8 to 0.10.1 (homebrew). pattern: run `redwoodctl localserve --profile dev` then after ~30s a Keychain dialog appears saying "redwoodctl wants to use tokens in Keychain". if I click "always allow" it still reappears later.

mac-bot: system note: macOS Keychain may present prompts when an app uses a keychain item and the code signature or path differs from when the item was created.

ux: did the homebrew install change the binary path? e.g., /opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl vs /usr/local/. Also are you running localserve from Finder/dock? GUI-launched binaries can behave differently.

tara: running from terminal. `which redwoodctl` -> /opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl. Token stored in Keychain with application label "redwoodctl" (I think redwoodctl v0.9 wrote it).

evan: can you show `security find-generic-password -s redwoodctl -g` (redacted output ok). curious about "creator" or "access" lists.

tara:
```
$ security find-generic-password -s redwoodctl -g
keychain: "/Users/tara/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db"
class: "lgenp"
attributes:
    0x00000007 <blob>="redwoodctl"
    "acct"="t-robot"
    "svce"="redwoodctl-token"
password: "(redacted)"
```
No explicit ACL printed.

ops: this smells like the CLI is rotating tokens and writing to Keychain repeatedly (new item each time) or trying to access with a different code signing identity. If the PID path or code-sign identity changes, Keychain enforces prompt. Also repeated access without caching could trigger popups.

ux: repro suggestion: run `REDWOOD_LOG=debug redwoodctl localserve` and watch for lines around auth refresh/rotate. Also check `redwoodctl auth status --verbose` to see expiry.

tara: logs:
```
[2026-03-10T14:02:10Z] auth: token expiry=2026-03-10T14:05:00Z
[2026-03-10T14:02:40Z] auth: refreshing token (silent)
[2026-03-10T14:02:40Z] keychain: write token -> success
[2026-03-10T14:03:10Z] keychain: read token -> prompt shown
[2026-03-10T14:03:40Z] auth: refreshing token (silent)
[2026-03-10T14:03:40Z] keychain: write token -> success
```
It keeps doing the refresh every 30s, and read attempts show prompt.

evan: 30s seems like a bug — refresh should be on expiry window (e.g., 5-10% of lifetime) or use backoff. Are these short-lived tokens?

tara: token TTL is 2m in our dev setup (we use short tokens to exercise rotation). but even so localserve shouldn't prompt repeatedly. it should refresh in the background without requiring UI.

ops: I suspect two things: 1) Keychain write uses SecItemAdd when item exists (should use SecItemUpdate), creating transient duplicates or different ACLs, and 2) SecItemCopyMatching may not be using kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain or correct query flags so macOS prompts. Code signature mismatch could also be it — homebrew upgrade replaced binary path (symlink) and Keychain associates allowed apps by path.

mac-bot: note: if an item is created with the app permission set to a specific binary path, and you later run a different binary (same name but different path), macOS will prompt. Use kSecAttrAccessGroup or add proper ACL that includes the app as trusted.

evan: quick workaround: run `security set-generic-password-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -s redwoodctl -a t-robot` to set partition list so non-interactive access allowed for code-signed tools (requires admin). Not perfect for users.

tara: tried that but it's admin-only and noisy. also for CI we don't want prompts.

ux: longer term fixes: - change token storage to prefer file-based $XDG_CONFIG_HOME with optional OS-specific protection; - when using Keychain, on writes use SecItemUpdate if item exists and preserve ACLs; - cache tokens in-memory and avoid read/write on every refresh; - respect a dev opt-in to keep tokens in plaintext file for local runs (with a clear warning).

evan: will submit PR to: 1) implement SecItemUpdate and a single token item; 2) add a 10s jitter + exponential backoff for refresh loops; 3) introduce env var REDWOOD_KEYCHAIN_STRICT=0 to skip secure keychain use for dev. Also will add an integration test that simulates short TTLs and verifies no repeated prompts.

ops: small security note — any option to bypass Keychain must be opt-in and documented; CI images should use machine-level token file with tight perms instead of bypassing.

tara: for now we set REDWOOD_KEYCHAIN_STRICT=0 in our dev env and switched to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME token file; localserve no longer prompts. filing ISSUE: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/678 - "macOS Keychain prompts on token refresh; use SecItemUpdate + reduce refresh frequency". added logs and repro steps.

evan: thanks! I'll tag mac leads and plan a small patch this week. appreciate the clear repro. :rocket:
